newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Treasury's Ciampi says time to cut rates.
newsitem.headline: Italy Treasury's Ciampi says time to cut rates.

text.p: Italy's treasury and budget minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview published on Tuesday that he believed conditions were right for a cut in interest rates in Italy and Europe.
Ciampi, a former central banker, told Rome's La Repubblica newspaper that falling inflation and privatisation helped establish conditions for economic growth in Italy.

"There is one point that is crucial, however, and that is real rates of interest. They are still too high in Europe and in Italy. The conditions exist for their fall," he said. Ciampi did not specify to which interest rates he was referring.
Following a consistent fall in inflation this year, many economists expect the Bank of Italy to cut the discount rate, which currently stands at 7.50 percent, by the end of the year.

The Bank of Italy has cut the discount rate twice this year, in July and October, both times by 75 basis points, and many economists expect a further cut after preliminary December inflation data are published later this month.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi has called on banks to cut interest rates they charge customers.
